tested.t1: tested on 2022 and 2024 county, court and soil and water races (MEDSL's copies of the Secretary's files)
tested.t2: tested on 2022 and 2024 races for this office
tested.u: untested: no past results for these offices are on file (the Secretary's files for city, school, township and hospital races have not been saved), so the method borrows its spread from county races

key.r: races by id, the state's prefix ("pre") taken off
key.c: candidates, favourite first: [name as filed, chance, median share, 80% low, 80% high]; a chance is a whole percent from 1 to 99, or ">99" (over 99 percent) or "<1" (under 1 percent); shares in tenths of a percent
key.eq: where nothing on the record separates the candidates: their one shared [chance, median, 80% low, 80% high], and "c" holds the names alone, in alphabetical order (the page says the record gives no reason to favour any of them)
key.s: seats when more than one (the chance is then of finishing among the winners)
key.v: expected voters in the race: [10th, 50th, 90th percentile]
key.x: which past races the method was tested on (a code of "tested")
key.sc: share of the expected vote counted when the model ran (absent before results)
key.t, m, k: the race's own run time, method version and kind where they differ from the file's
key.about: the newest run's inputs and method in plain words ("ran": when the model last ran, though no race may have changed; "t" at the top: when the newest change was made)
key.st: the count's state when the model ran, where it is not "pre": counting (some of the race's precincts in) or done (every precinct in, the counties' last absentee ballots perhaps still to come); absent: none of the race's precincts counted yet
key.k values: pre: the forecast before results; live: the election-night model, from the votes counted so far
key.mg: the likely margin of the top two: the first candidate's share less the second's (the first two of "c"), [median, 80% low, 80% high], in tenths of a percentage point; a range below 0 means the second could finish ahead (absent where several are elected or nothing on the record separates the candidates)
key.ro: where the law asks for more than half the votes: the chance that no candidate passes half (a runoff, or the legislature decides), as a chance cell

about.backtest: Sized by the backtests run on October 10, 2026.
about.district: District races add their precincts' leans by expected votes, then a sitting member's edge (about 1.1 points), a regional swing and the district's own error, each sized on the 2022 and 2024 results.
about.environment: In 11 states, U.S. Senate polls by members of AAPOR's Transparency Initiative have Democrats running 3.6 points ahead of Kamala Harris's 2024 share of the two-party vote. Applied to Minnesota's 2024 presidential result (52.2% DFL of the two-party vote) and moved a little by Minnesota's own member polls, a generic 2026 Minnesota contest stands near 55.8% DFL, give or take about 2.7 points.
about.lean: Each precinct's lean is its DFL share against the state's in these past contests: 2024: the presidential and U.S. Senate races; 2022: the governor's, secretary of state's, attorney general's and state auditor's races (presidential contests weighted 15 times; each older election 0.45 times the next).
about.nonpartisan: Nonpartisan races: a seat's holder is expected to take about 58% against one challenger, as in the 2022 and 2024 county, court and soil and water races; a party's published endorsement counts for a little, more where the place leans to that party; where the record names no holder and no endorsement, chances are equal.
about.not_used: Campaign money and Census figures are not used before Election Day: neither has been tested on past races yet.
about.position: Ballot position: each name's share of voters who see it first, rebuilt from Minnesota's rotation rule with 2024's registration counts (an estimate: the counties draw the starting order by lot, and it is not on file); town ballots list names alphabetically, so there the first name is known.
about.turnout: Expected voters: each precinct's 2022 ballots, grown with its registration since 2022, less the share that skipped that office in 2022 (roll-off).
about.untested: City, school, township and hospital races are untested: no past results for them are on file, so their spread is borrowed from county races.
